The Energy Innovation Challenge (EIC), sponsored by The AES Corporation, is an energy case competition that brings together graduate students to tackle real-world challenges shaping the future of the energy industry. This case competition allows teams of students to engage with industry professionals and simulate a pitch in a corporate environment, building problem-solving, presentation, and teamwork skills.

What we are looking for in applicants:

- Students from areas such as engineering, public policy, finance, sustainability, business, environmental studies, or related disciplines

- A strong interest in the energy sector and the future of innovation

- Passion for solving complex challenges at the intersection of technology, business, policy, and sustainability

Applicants should meet the following criteria:

- Team Size: Teams must consist of 3 to 5 students

- Education Level: All applicants must be currently enrolled in a graduate degree program or an equivalent program

- Interdisciplinary Requirement: Teams must include students from at least 2 different degree programs

- Academic Institution:  All team members must be enrolled at the same university

Why Participate?

- Connect your studies to your current and future career

- Network with energy professionals

- Engage with a unique company that works across the energy value chain

- Create solutions to help solve the energy industry’s biggest current issues

Challenge Prize:

1st place: $10,000 to the team and $1,000 to the charity of the team’s choice.
2nd place: $5,000 to the team and $1,000 to the charity of the team’s choice.
Both first and second place teams win an interview conversation with AES hiring teams .

QUALIFICATIONS :  Applicant must have a high school diploma or GED; must be able to successfully complete the Company’s lineman apprentice training program; have ability to perform construction and maintenance work on poles, towers, other overhead structures and underground equipment as required; must be capable of operating power equipment associated with work performed in Lines Field Operations; must meet standards for and be able to complete requirements for a Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) as defined by the Commercial Motor Vehicle Safety Act of 1986.  The applicant must pass the EEI Construction & Skilled Trades (CAST) test and the Lineman Physical Abilities Test (PAT).  In addition, must be willing to work from any of the Company’s operating centers, in inclement weather or emergencies and meet service commitments.  Other general qualifications such as physical fitness, attendance, safety and performance records will be considered.

1.   Setting or removing poles or steel towers; installing and removing any associated equipment such as transformers, voltage regulators, street light regulators, capacitors, cutouts, lightning arresters, disconnects, oil switches, reclosers, etc.;
2.   May be required at any time to drive or operate line truck, digger or any aerial truck;
3.   Stringing conductors, splicing and correcting sagging wires;
4.   Making safe and adequate rigging of blocks, gin poles, etc. necessary to raise or lower any associated line equipment or material; assisting line foreman in directing the operator of a truck, winch, crane, etc. used to raise or lower the equipment or material;

7.   Placing and clearing temporary grounds on de-energized conductors.
8.   Perform underground commercial and residential work.

Must be willing to work rotating shifts including weekends and holidays.

The Senior Internal Auditor plays a key role in helping safeguard the organization's financial, digital, and operational integrity. In this highly visible position, you will lead and execute complex audit and advisory engagements with a high degree of independence, applying professional judgment and recognized internal auditing standards. You will evaluate financial controls, systems, and operational and digital processes to identify existing and emerging risks, control opportunities, and ways to strengthen business performance.
This role contributes to the Company's Sarbanes-Oxley compliance efforts, helps develop practical risk mitigation solutions, and supports initiatives that enhance and protect organizational value. The Senior Internal Auditor partners with stakeholders across the business, communicates clear and actionable insights, drives the timely resolution of audit issues, and supports the growth and development of team members through coaching and knowledge sharing.

Why Join Us?
This role offers a unique opportunity to gain broad exposure to the organization's operations, leadership teams, and strategic priorities. As part of a collaborative Internal Audit function, you will work across diverse business areas, contribute to meaningful improvements, and continuously expand your expertise in operational, financial, compliance, and technology-related risks.
We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where diverse perspectives are valued, professional growth is encouraged, and continuous learning is supported through challenging assignments, collaboration, and development opportunities.

Role of the Senior Internal Auditor
We are looking for a collaborative, analytical, and detail-oriented Senior Internal Auditor to join our team. In this role, you will plan and execute risk-based operational audits and advisory reviews, assess the design and effectiveness of controls, and translate complex analyses into meaningful business insights.
The ideal candidate enjoys solving problems, working across functions, and building relationships with stakeholders at all levels of the organization. You will have opportunities to influence business processes, contribute to risk management initiatives, and help drive continuous improvement across the company.
This is a hybrid position that requires regular work from an office and is preferably based in Salt Lake City, Utah; Louisville, Colorado; Indianapolis, Indiana or Houston, Texas. The position includes domestic and international travel opportunities based on business and audit needs.

Key Responsibilities

- Lead and execute comprehensive, risk-based audits of operational processes, including scoping, risk assessment, audit program development, walkthroughs, testing, and reporting.

- Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of operational, financial, compliance, technology-enabled, and risk management controls.

- Identify root causes, assess business impact, and partner with management to develop practical, risk-based recommendations.

- Prepare clear, concise, and well-supported workpapers, findings, and reports that meet internal quality standards and professional auditing requirements.

- Communicate audit objectives, status updates, emerging concerns, and results to stakeholders in a timely and constructive manner.

- Build effective relationships with cross-functional stakeholders and support sustainable process improvements and corrective actions.

- Collaborate with audit team members and business partners throughout engagements, proactively sharing information and contributing to a positive, solutions-focused environment.

- Monitor remediation commitments and evaluate supporting evidence to determine whether identified risks have been appropriately addressed.

- Provide coaching, feedback, and day-to-day guidance to team members to support their development and success.

- Contribute to annual risk assessments, audit planning activities, continuous improvement initiatives, and the enhancement of audit methodologies and tools.

- Support Sarbanes-Oxley compliance activities and coordinate with internal and external stakeholders, as applicable.

- Stay informed about industry developments, regulatory changes, emerging risks, data analytics, and evolving internal audit practices.

- Participate in special projects and advisory engagements that contribute to organizational objectives and professional growth opportunities.

Qualifications
We recognize that candidates may bring relevant experience through a variety of career paths. If your background aligns closely with the role, we encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every preferred qualification.

- Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, Engineering, Economics, or a related field.

- Approximately 3 to 5 years of experience in internal audit, external audit, risk management, operational processes, compliance, or a related area. Equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered.

- Professional certification such as CIA, CPA, or an equivalent designation is preferred. Candidates actively pursuing certification are encouraged to apply.

- Experience within a Big 4 accounting firm, internal audit consulting practice, or a complex multinational organization is preferred.

- Demonstrated ability to independently manage and execute complex assignments while balancing multiple priorities.

- Strong analytical, critical thinking, problem-solving, and root-cause analysis skills, with attention to detail and evidence quality.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex concepts clearly to diverse audiences.

- Proven ability to build trusted relationships, collaborate effectively across teams, value diverse perspectives, and influence outcomes without direct authority.

- Experience mentoring, coaching, reviewing work, or supporting the development of others is preferred.

- Familiarity with Microsoft Office and audit, analytics, visualization, governance, risk, or compliance tools is preferred.

As part of the Engineering Department, the High Voltage Engineering team delivers preconstruction engineering and construction/commissioning engineering for High Voltage facilities associated with renewable energy power plants.

We are currently looking for a substation or transmission engineer to oversee the execution of high voltage projects located across the country but heavily in the Western United States portfolio (Texas, California, Arizona, Utah, Nevada, and Hawaii). The engineer for this position should enjoy the versatility of technical tasks with a strong focus on understanding grid integration requirements for renewables and data centers. The role is that of an owner’s engineer to oversee high voltage designs from EPC firms contracted to design and build the high voltage facilities for our projects to ensure it meets interconnection and commercial requirements, and to provide technical oversight during the construction. Strong experience in detailed substation design and/or transmission line design preferred.

A ideal candidate would be one who can coordinate deliverables through internal and external parties, has a wide breadth of technical skills (e.g. P&C design, physical substation design, modelling, interconnection, t-line design), passionate about continual learning and working as part of a team.

This position is open to non-senior candidates who are passionate about learning, demonstrate extreme ownership and have a demonstrated history of growing in rapid environments. Listed below are the differences between seniors and non-senior positions.

We are open to considering U.S. remote-based candidates, preferably located in the Pacific (PST) or Mountain (MST) time zones.

Principal Duties and Responsibilities:

- Responsible for oversight of EPC contractor engineering design and construction activities for Solar, Wind, and BESS collector high voltage substations and transmission lines (35kV to 500kV).

- Establish and maintain relationships with high voltage contractors.

- Review Substation EPC designs for compliance with interconnection agreement requirements, applicable reliability standards, standard industry practices, etc.

- Provide design review and advice on any issues that appear technically incorrect or inconsistent with project documentation.

- Coordinate the review power system studies such as load flows, short circuits, harmonics, TOV, insulation coordination, etc.

- Direct coordination with Interconnection Providers(utilities) to design collector substations to include Transmission Provider requirements and internal stakeholders while including AES specifications.

- Coordinate Generation Tie line or Transmission line design with EPC and internal stakeholders to ensure it remains within the project requirements.

- Support role during substation commissioning by reviewing apparatus testing and coordinating testing with utility and ISO.

- Growth opportunity for a leadership role within the engineering team.

- Work with a project team including real estate, permitting, interconnection, attorneys, finance, and construction in the field.

- Travel and fieldwork 25%. Projects are located across the country but this position will support wind (anywhere) and PV/BESS (west coast).

Minimum Qualifications

- B.S. Electrical Engineering or other engineering disciplines.

Senior Engineer :

- 7+ years of a combination of technical design experience. This can include substation design experience (either Physical, P&C), Transmission line design, power flow/studies.

- Proficient in readings control schematics for HV breakers, Main Power Transformers, etc.

- Mature understanding of grid integration requirements for renewables.

- More advanced knowledge of power system modeling such as load flow, insulation coordination, grounding, arc-flash, TOV, harmonics, etc.

Non-senior:

- 4+ years of a combination of technical design experience. This can include substation design experience (either Physical, P&C), Transmission line design, power flow/studies.

- Advanced in readings control schematics for HV breakers, Main Power Transformers, etc.

- Basic understanding of grid integration requirements for renewables.

- Basic Knowledge of power system modeling such as load flow, insulation coordination, grounding, arc-flash, TOV, harmonics, etc.

- 2+ years of project engineering experience in an HV related role.

- Strong communication skills and ability to lead technical discussions among HV EPCs, Power Utilities, and internal stakeholders.

- Strong organizational skills and ability to prioritize projects and tasks.

Desired Skills and Experience

- Project Management experience handling HV EPCs.

- PE Licensure in any of these states: Arizona, California, Hawaii, Nevada, or Utah.

- Technical lead experience coordinating engineering packages such as IFPs and IFCs.

- Experience with ETAP, PSLF, PSS/E or PLS-CADD

- Experience in relay system testing.

- Experience in SCADA controls and architecture.

- B.S. Electrical Engineering or higher with emphasis on Power Systems.

- Participate in formalized AES-specific learning opportunities to further your knowledge toward accelerating the responsible energy transition

- Network with peers, AES leaders, and like-minded employees through dedicated events, lunch-and-learns, and speaker series

- Actively engage in open discussions to help identify ways AES can better prepare for the future of energy

Requirements:

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, or a related field

- Coursework in power systems, circuits, or electric machines

- Problem-solving mindset and willingness to learn

- Ability to communicate clearly, verbally and in writing

- Exposure to power-flow or short-circuit software (PSS®E, TARA, ASPEN, CAPE, DSA Tools, or similar)

- Familiarity with the NERC/FERC/PJM/MISO regulatory landscape

The Director of Field Operations is responsible for the safe, reliable, and cost-effective operation of AES's renewable energy portfolio across the Eastern United States and Puerto Rico. This role provides strategic leadership for field operations, operational performance, regional execution, financial stewardship, and continuous improvement initiatives that drive operational excellence and support long-term business success.

Safety First | Initiative-Taker | Innovative Thinker | Driven by Excellence | Collaborative Teammate | Accountable Leader

The ideal candidate brings strong technical, financial, and leadership experience within the energy industry, along with demonstrated success supporting the safe and effective operation of utility-scale and distributed energy assets. They also possess a solid understanding of the commercial and operational aspects of energy facilities.

We are open to considering U.S. remote-based candidates located in the EST time zone

Key Responsabilities

- Lead the safe and effective execution of solar, battery energy storage (BESS), and wind field operations across the Eastern United States and Puerto Rico.

- Oversee the safe execution of Operations and Maintenance (O&M) activities across U.S. sites utilizing third-party O&M providers.

- Develop and implement strategies that optimize costs while maintaining strong safety, reliability, and operational performance standards.

- Partner with Asset Management, Finance, Commercial, and other cross-functional teams to maximize asset performance and profitability.

- Provide oversight and accountability for fleet availability, reliability, safety, operational performance, and cost management through clearly defined performance metrics and KPIs.

- Drive continuous improvement and standardization initiatives using operational data, analytics, and emerging technologies to improve maintenance effectiveness, workforce productivity, asset performance, and reduce unplanned downtime.

- Lead U.S. O&M business budget planning in partnership with regional Field Operations and Asset Management teams.

- Develop and execute long-term workforce, capital, maintenance, and resource strategies that support portfolio growth and operational excellence.

- Establish and maintain performance, cost, staffing, and productivity benchmarks to support informed business decisions and operational competitiveness.

- Support the development of O&M cost estimates for new projects within the U.S. portfolio.

- Provide coaching, mentorship, performance feedback, and development opportunities that promote employee growth and engagement.

- Foster an inclusive, collaborative, and safety-focused culture where team members feel valued, respected, and empowered to contribute their best work.

- Serve as a key operational representative to senior leadership, investors, lenders, joint venture partners, customers, and other stakeholders.

- Communicate operational and financial performance results to executive leadership and external stakeholders.

- Lead the fleet vehicle program for the O&M organization.

- Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning, talent development, and strategic hiring initiatives.

Minimum Qualifications

- 10 -15 years of experience leading renewable energy operations, asset management, maintenance, power generation, or related technical operations functions, typically gained through progressively responsible leadership roles.

- Bachelor's degree in engineering or related field.

- Experience leading multi-site operations teams through managers and supervisors in geographically dispersed environments.

- Ability to interpret and understand equipment and facility schematics.

- Knowledge of systems, processes, and standards related to the operation and maintenance of utility-scale solar plants and electrical systems, including applicable IEEE, NERC, OSHA, NFPA 70E, Lockout/Tagout, Grounding, and related standards.

- Familiarity with SCADA, DAS, remote monitoring systems, and associated operational protocols.

- Demonstrated commitment to fostering a strong safety culture and maintaining a safe work environment.

- Alignment with AES values, including Safety First, Highest Standards, and All Together.

- Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and other business productivity tools.

- Ability to travel up to 30% as business needs require.

Preferred Qualifications

- Advanced degree (MBA, Master's degree, or similar graduate-level education).

- Experience with P&L ownership and financial accountability.

- Experience supporting operations and maintenance activities for thermal generation assets.

- Demonstrated ability to lead through complexity, drive results, and build high-performing teams.

- Experience managing utility-scale solar, BESS, and wind portfolios.

- Experience leading remote and geographically dispersed teams.

- Experience managing third-party service providers and performance-based contracts.

- Experience presenting to executive leadership teams, boards, investors, lenders, or other external stakeholders.

The High Voltage Engineering team provides pre-construction, construction, and commissioning engineering support for high-voltage facilities associated with renewable energy power plants, including solar, wind, and battery energy storage projects. These facilities range from 35 kV through 500 kV. We are seeking a dynamic, collaborative, and technically strong Senior Protection and Control Engineer to support high-voltage substation projects. This role is an excellent opportunity for an engineer with strong protection and control expertise who also values collaboration with EPC partners, power utilities, and internal project teams. The selected engineer will lead protection and control activities from design development through execution, commissioning, and post-energization support for greenfield and brownfield substations across AES Clean Energy projects.

We are open to considering U.S. remote-based candidates, preferably located in the MST or EST.

Principal Duties and Responsibilities

- Lead protection and control engineering activities for AES Clean Energy high-voltage substations supporting solar, wind, and battery energy storage projects, with voltage levels ranging from 35 kV to 500 kV.

- Provide technical leadership throughout the project lifecycle, including design development, engineering review, construction support, commissioning, energization, and post-energization support.

- Review protection and control drawings, protection philosophies, relay settings, short-circuit studies, coordination studies, grounding studies, EMT studies, and related technical reports.

- Evaluate short-circuit study results for generation interconnections and provide actionable feedback to EPC partners to support protection design and coordination.

- Apply strong knowledge of protection coordination, time-current characteristics, SEL protection and automation products, and engineering tools such as SEL software, ETAP, and PowerFactory.

- Support technical review and interpretation of equipment testing for high- and medium-voltage circuit breakers, main power transformers, instrument transformers, surge arresters, and grounding systems.

- Coordinate NERC PRC compliance activities across multiple projects and work with EPCs, utilities, and internal stakeholders to support applicable standards and reporting requirements.

- Lead efforts to standardize protection and control practices, philosophies, templates, and lessons learned across projects and applications.

- Support root-cause analysis for site events during commissioning, energization, or operations, and incorporate lessons learned into protection and control standards.

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including development, execution, operations and maintenance, and asset management, to improve project outcomes and support long-term operational value.

- Stay current with evolving protection technologies, OEM guidance, utility requirements, and applicable industry standards, including NERC PRC standards and IEEE guidelines.

- Mentor associate engineers and peer engineers, support technical knowledge sharing, and contribute to leadership development within the engineering organization.

- Travel to project sites, vendor facilities, and commissioning locations as needed; anticipated travel and field work is approximately 25%.

Minimum Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering with an emphasis in power systems.

- Minimum of 5 years of demonstrated experience in protection and control engineering for high-voltage substations or renewable generation facilities.

- Experience with SEL protection and automation products is required.

- Strong understanding of power system fundamentals, protection principles, relay coordination, and substation control schemes.

- Experience reviewing or supporting high-voltage equipment testing procedures, test results, and commissioning documentation.

- Familiarity with communication standards and protocols such as IEC 61850, DNP3, Modbus, and related substation automation applications.

- Ability to read and interpret electrical single-line diagrams, DC schematics, protection and control drawings, and substation equipment wiring diagrams.

- Strong communication skills, including the ability to lead technical discussions with EPCs, utilities, consultants, and internal stakeholders.

- Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage priorities across multiple projects and tasks.

- Ability to support project engineering activities during substation design, construction, commissioning, and energization.

Desired Skills and Experience

- Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related power systems discipline.

- Substation design experience in physical design, protection and control design, or both.

- Experience with SCADA systems, controls architecture, and substation automation design.

- Experience developing or supporting hardware-in-the-loop testing environments for protection relays, SCADA systems, and related substation equipment.

- Project management experience coordinating multiple consultants, EPCs, and project stakeholders concurrently.

AES has been  ranked #1 by BloombergNEF  in renewable energy sales to corporations in the US and Americas for five consecutive years, providing electricity for  millions of people worldwide.

If you're ready to be part of a company that's not just adapting to change, but driving it, AES is the place for you. We're not just building a more sustainable future ,  we're powering it. Apply now and energize your career with a true leader in global energy.

At AES Renewables & Power (AES R&P) , we're accelerating the energy transition by delivering innovative solutions that power the world's fastest-growing industries. As a Developer, Gas Generation , you'll play a key role in developing generation projects that enable large-load customers—including data centers—to access reliable, scalable energy as part of integrated Powered Land Solutions.

This is an exciting opportunity to work at the intersection of project development, infrastructure, and commercial strategy while collaborating with industry experts across engineering, development, finance, legal, construction, and commercial teams. You'll help bring complex energy projects from concept to construction and contribute to solutions that are transforming how customers access power.

If you're energized by solving complex challenges, collaborating across disciplines, and making a tangible impact on the future of energy, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Do
As a Developer, Gas Generation, you'll lead the development of natural gas generation projects that support integrated energy solutions for large commercial and industrial customers.
You'll collaborate with multidisciplinary teams throughout the full project lifecycle—from early-stage development through construction handoff—to ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, and successfully.

Your responsibilities will include:

- Leading gas generation project development from site identification through construction support.

- Partnering with Commercial, Data Center Development, Renewable Generation Development, Solutions Engineering, and other internal teams to develop integrated Powered Land Solutions.

- Evaluating project feasibility by coordinating siting, fuel supply, interconnection, infrastructure, and permitting strategies.

- Managing project schedules, budgets, forecasts, financial models, and development risk registers.

- Coordinating pipeline identification, utility engagement, and fuel supply strategy while supporting commercial negotiations.

- Working closely with internal and external stakeholders—including engineering consultants, permitting agencies, landowners, utility companies, customers, and contractors—to advance project milestones.

- Supporting discretionary permitting efforts, public meetings, regulatory engagement, and environmental diligence.

- Coordinating engineering, site due diligence, land activities, and infrastructure planning to keep projects on schedule.

- Managing contracts and ensuring compliance with key project agreements, including site control, fuel supply, and commercial contracts.

- Identifying project risks, recommending mitigation strategies, and communicating project updates to leadership and stakeholders.

- Supporting project financing due diligence and ensuring accurate project documentation within AES systems.

- Leading successful project handoffs to Construction once development milestones have been achieved.

- Representing AES professionally while building strong relationships with customers, partners, regulatory agencies, and local communities.

What You'll Bring
We're looking for someone who enjoys working in a collaborative environment, can manage multiple priorities, and is passionate about delivering innovative energy infrastructure projects. You may be a great fit if you have:

- Experience developing natural gas generation or other large-scale energy infrastructure projects.

- A bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Finance, Economics, Environmental Science, or another related field.

- Knowledge of project development, permitting, utility coordination, interconnection, pipeline infrastructure, and commercial contracting.

- Experience working with fuel supply strategies, utilities, pipeline operators, or integrated energy infrastructure.

- Familiarity with gas generation technologies.

- The ability to collaborate across technical, commercial, and customer-facing teams to develop practical energy solutions.

- Experience supporting data centers, large-load customers, powered land projects, or similar infrastructure developments (preferred).

- Strong project management, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

- Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to communicate effectively across diverse audiences.

- The ability to balance multiple projects in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.

- Willingness to travel as projects and business needs require.

POSITION SCOPE :
Under general guidance is responsible and accountable for the continuous safe, stable, reliable, economical, environmentally correct operation, and/or maintenance of an assigned functional area of responsibility within Grid Operations for the AES Indianapolis Distribution area.  Provides supervision, leadership, and training to others through day-to-day contact.  Provides technical advice and counsel for difficult projects.  Prioritizes, directs, monitors, and evaluates performance of direct reports within the reporting organization.  Prepares, controls, and administers project budgets to achieve maximum business results relating to overall performance, cost efficiency and reliability.
The Grid Coordinator is responsible for complying with NERC, FERC, RFC, IURC and MISO requirements and directing field personnel through switching operations involving the mainline distribution system and the Bulk Electric Transmission System.  Will provide assistance to Transmission System Operations during normal and emergency operations as conditions may require.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

- Makes complex operating, engineering and economic decisions involving the restoration of customer’s service following system emergencies and coordinates the distribution system effort with the Transmission Control Center and the Distribution Operations Control Center.

- Maintains a work environment that promotes good customer service, striving to economically meet customer requests within the timeframe requested.

- Maintains a safe, professional work environment that offers employees challenging and meaningful work and opportunities to develop their skills and talents

- Directs the preparation and execution of contingency plans for operating the distribution system during natural disasters, civil disturbances and in other critical situations

- Directs, plans, and arranges work schedules to meet both unscheduled and regular work; participates in long-range Company planning with other departments and outside the Customer Operations

- Directs departmental personnel regarding assignments; reviews records, reports and analyses related to the department’s work; participates in such work as may be required to meet normal and emergency conditions

- Directs Grid Operations office personnel representing the Company to the customer in all matters regarding Company business and operation of the customer’s service during those hours when the main offices are closed

- Works closely with the Customer Service Team during regular working hours

- Forecasts a significant portion of the operation and maintenance budget and subsequent control of those expenses

- Receive, analyze, schedule, route, direct and assign emergency and routine work to maintain continuity of electric service to customers;  determine capabilities of substations and circuits so as not to overload conductors, distribution transformers, underground risers, breaker current transformers, substation transformers, voltage regulators and line reclosers, including tabulating connected KVA to be transferred, calculating connected amperes, and applying proper load factors for day and night peak loads;

- Initiates and issues the necessary switching orders and operations to repair and restore electric service continuity on the overhead and underground distribution systems, including customer switchgear and breakers served at distribution voltage levels, and requires knowledge of transformers, voltage regulators, circuit breakers, capacitors, switchgear and reclosers; directs work on underground distribution  areas and complexes, the operation of single and three phase underground feeds and pad mounted transformers;

- Reads, interprets, analyzes, and corrects distribution and street lighting maps; uses a basic understanding of line fuse coordination while monitoring and reporting incorrect applications and a full understanding of distribution circuit and street lighting operations in order to use the Outage Management System, office maps and descriptive data received from the field to analyze various trouble information to help determine the probable point of trouble where a circuit is faulted or open

- Interprets and relays maps and operating record information to assist field personnel and provide shared safety responsibilities

- Compiles and prepares reports incident to Distribution Operations

- Maintains a Grid Operations log, recording abnormal conditions, outages on the distribution system and their causes; authorizes and records “hold cards” for safety of workers when taking out or putting into service distribution and street lighting circuits or equipment

- Receives, relays and records intra-company, inter-company, police, and fire department communications

- Performs timekeeping and payroll work and processes case jobs and damage claims; and

- Operates two-way radio in accordance with FCC regulations and AES Indiana Distribution Operations working rules.

- In addition to the primary duties listed above, the employee may be called upon to perform other work as circumstances require.

- Must know and comply with all Company safety and health policies and procedures applicable to work performance.

- Directs field switching operations performed by authorized personnel including Substation Inspectors/Switchmen, Substation Mechanics, Electricians, Linemen, Relay/SCADA Specialists, Troublemen and any other classification that may be required to operate equipment on the bulk electric system.

- Assists in monitoring system conditions watching for abnormalities or other conditions that could affect the reliability of the electric system; when such conditions are detected, the Grid Coordinator may recommend to department management taking immediate action to remedy the situation and will direct Operations personnel in those actions.

QUALIFICATIONS:
Basic Requirements:

- High school graduate.

- High degree of electrical and mechanical aptitude.

- Available for all System Operations shifts (24-7).

- Ability to pass NERC Certification exam within 6 months.

Preferred Skills:

- Accredited post secondary education in an engineering or technology related field.

- Current NERC Certification.

- Electric Utility experience in transmission and/or distribution operations.

- Computer proficiency and effective verbal and written communication skills are requirements.

- Ability to work in a real-time operations environment on all shifts and as a team member.

- Understanding of power substation equipment, power system electrical fundamentals, and the ability to interpret substation one-line diagrams and electrical schematics.

- Proficient in the English Language.

- Electric utility job related experience or training.

Transmission and Distribution environmental project permitting and management.

Under the general guidance of the Director of Global Environmental Affairs, the Senior Environmental Specialist will be responsible for:

- Leading all aspects of and handling environmental permitting activities for a large number of electricity transmission and distribution (T&D) construction projects for AES Indiana and AES Ohio. Projects can include transmission and distribution lines (new and rebuilt), substations (new and expansion), laydown yards, storage facilities, and other associated infrastructure projects.

- Supporting and reviewing environmental permitting activities for electricity generation projects.

- Preparing and submitting Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and coordinating qualified environmental consultants for various environmental services, including but not limited to: Phase 1 and Phase 2 Environmental Site Assessments, natural resources, ecological, and cultural resources site assessment and permit applicability evaluations, constructability assessments, permit package preparation and transfer to compliance team.

- Developing or enhancing management and permitting programs and standards for prioritizing, assessing, and obtaining permits, including both external and internal permitting support.

- Providing environmental due diligence, emergency response, and waste support to the T&D teams, which could include determining environmental site conditions, coordinating soil sampling and analysis, evaluating results to determine remediation needs, special instructions for design or construction, pre-approvals, and coordination of disposal of equipment or contaminated soil with appropriate vendors and disposal sites.

- Interacting with local, state, and federal government agencies regarding associated environmental matters of T&D projects.

- Interacting and coordinating with the T&D Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) Analyst and T&D personnel and contractors to ensure that permit compliance requirements are fully communicated, including inspections, recordkeeping, reporting, and permit termination.

- Additional responsibilities include supporting AES Indiana Planning, Siting, and Outreach teams with various projects and initiatives.

Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, engineering, or related science-related field from an accredited college/university.

- Minimum of seven (7) years of recent environmental construction permitting or oversight of permitting in Indiana and Ohio.

- Experience, knowledge, and familiarity with environmental construction permitting, including CWA 404; CWA 401; nationwide permits; stormwater construction permitting; floodway/floodplain permitting; drainage easement requirements; and local permitting requirements. This includes experience, knowledge, and familiarity with underlying regulations and laws applicable to these types of permits.

- Experience, knowledge, and familiarity with various regulatory consultations, including federal and state rare, threatened, and endangered (RTE) species, Migratory Bird Treaty Act (MBTA), Endangered Species Act (ESA), Bald and Golden Eagle Protection Act (BGEPA), and cultural resources management, including the application of the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA).

- Experience, knowledge, and familiarity with the American Society of Testing Materials (ASTM) Standard Practice ASTM E1527-21. This includes experience, knowledge, and familiarity with underlying regulations and laws applicable to these types of permits.

- Ability to work under pressure within deadlines and while handling multiple priorities. Strong communication skills and ability to interact with a diverse group. Self-driven, results-oriented with a clear focus on high-quality outcomes and business success. Proficiency with MS Office Suite.

- Willingness to work in a union environment; motivated self-starter who can function with minimum supervision; valid Indiana or Ohio driver’s license.

Preferred:

- Master’s degree in environmental science, engineering, or related science-related field from an accredited college/university.

- Experience in environmental construction permitting specific to electricity T&D and renewable energy.

- Experience working with the City of Indianapolis and obtaining drainage permits through the Department of Business and Neighborhood Services.

- Experience in land acquisition environmental due diligence and CERCLA is preferred; experience in RCRA and waste management.

Primary Location: Indianapolis, Indiana, or Dayton, Ohio. Some travel between the Indianapolis, IN area and the Dayton, OH area required.

Director, Safety – AES Indiana & AES Ohio

Indianapolis, IN and/or Dayton, OH with regular travel to operational sites across Indiana and Ohio. Hybrid/On-site presence expected based on business needs.

COO, US Utilities

Position Summary
The Safety Director leads health & safety strategy and execution for AES Indiana and AES Ohio across Generation, Transmission & Distribution (T&D), operational/field sites, and all Construction - including Growth projects and programmatic capital programs . This leader is accountable for building and sustaining a strong safety culture, ensuring safety compliance, strengthening serious incident prevention, and improving health & safety performance through standardized systems, disciplined governance, and field-focused leadership.
This role partners closely with Operations leaders, T&D, Generation, Program/Project teams, Central Operations, HR, Legal, Supply Chain, Finance, and the enterprise EHS Center of Expertise (CoE) to ensure AES’s safety management system is implemented consistently while enabling local execution excellence and risk reduction across both company and contractor workforces.

Scope

- Two regulated electric utilities with diverse operational risk profiles

- Coverage includes:
- Power generation facilities and associated operational sites

- T&D field operations (line work, substations, vegetation, construction)

- Fleet, warehouses, service centers, storm response operations

- Contractor and vendor workforces supporting O&M and capital delivery

- All safety oversight for Construction across both utilities , including:
- Growth projects (ongoing and new generation as applicable, interconnections, substations, large load enablement, major reliability upgrades)

- Programmatic programs (Smart Grid,  system hardening, reconductoring, substation upgrades, fleet/facilities projects)

- Major contractor mobilizations, EPC/GC-led work, and multi-site execution

Key Outcomes / Success Measures

- Sustained improvement in serious injury and fatality prevention performance (SIP) and critical risk control verification

- Strong compliance performance with OSHA and state/local requirements (no significant findings; timely corrective actions)

- Improved leading indicators: field observations, hazard reporting, corrective action closure, training completion, contractor compliance

- High-quality investigations and learning dissemination with measurable recurrence reduction

- Increased consistency of health & safety standards, tools, and routines across both utilities and across capital delivery portfolios

Key Responsibilities
1) Safety Leadership & Culture

- Lead a “safety-first” culture across Generation, T&D, and Construction, reinforcing visible field leadership and consistent expectations.

- Coach operational and project leaders on safety leadership behaviors, accountability, and decision-making under risk.

- Establish and sustain effective engagement routines: site visits, safety stand-downs, leadership briefings, and field verification of critical controls.

2) Serious Incident Prevention & Critical Risk Management

- Own and drive serious injury/fatality prevention strategy and execution, including critical risk control verification.

- Ensure high-risk work is planned and executed with effective controls (energized work and switching, confined space, working at heights, lifting/rigging, excavation, traffic control, contractor work).

- Strengthen permit-to-work and work authorization processes where applicable.

3) Safety Management System, Governance & Assurance

- Implement and continuously improve the safety management system locally in alignment with enterprise standards and the EHS CoE.

- Lead audit/assessment programs, management reviews, and corrective action governance with strong follow-through and transparency.

- Establish data-driven performance management (dashboards, trend analysis, leading/lagging indicator reviews).

4) Incident Reporting, Investigations & Learning

- Ensure timely reporting, classification, investigation, and closeout of incidents and near-misses.

- Lead/oversee investigations for serious events using established methodologies; ensure high-quality root cause analysis and actionable corrective actions.

- Translate lessons learned into updated procedures, training, and field communications across both utilities and the construction portfolio.

5) Construction Health & Safety Leadership (Growth Projects & Programmatic Programs)

- Own and lead health & safety governance for all construction and capital delivery work across AES Indiana and AES Ohio, including growth and programmatic portfolios.

- Partner with Program Management, Engineering, T&D Construction, Generation project teams, Supply Chain, and contractors to embed  health & safety requirements into project planning, design reviews, contracting, mobilization, and execution .

- Ensure consistent application of construction health & safety controls (pre-task planning/JHAs, permits, work zones/traffic control, lifting/rigging plans, energized work boundaries, excavation controls, subcontractor management).

- Establish field verification routines for large projects/programs (site walks, audits, leading indicator reviews, stop-work reinforcement) and ensure corrective actions are closed with discipline.

- Lead serious event readiness for projects: escalation protocols, incident response, investigation standards, and lessons-learned deployment across the portfolio.

- Strengthen contractor qualification, onboarding, and performance management, including clear expectations, KPIs, and consequences for non-compliance.

6) Contractor Safety & Operational Risk Controls

- Build and enforce contractor health & safety requirements, including onboarding, qualification, field oversight, and performance management.

- Include construction contractors and project/program vendors in the contractor governance model, with clear onboarding, field oversight, and performance routines.

- Partner with Supply Chain and project leaders to embed health & safety requirements into contracting, mobilization, and project execution.

- Drive consistent application of job hazard analysis (JHA), pre-job briefs, stop-work authority, and field verification across O&M and construction.

7) Training, Competency & Workforce Readiness

- Ensure health & safety training, competency frameworks, and qualification processes are in place for employees and contractors.

- Partner with Operations, Construction leadership, and HR to strengthen onboarding, refresher training, leadership development, and compliance training completion.

- Support emergency preparedness and drill programs (including storm response readiness and construction incident readiness).

- Serve as the primary health & safety interface with regulators as needed (OSHA, state agencies), including inspections, inquiries, and corrective action plans.

- Partner with Legal and Communications on regulatory matters, reporting, and external stakeholder engagement.

- Participate in industry and peer utility forums as appropriate.

- Lead, develop, and align the safety organization across both utilities; build bench strength and succession plans.

- Create clear role expectations, operating rhythm, and performance management for safety team members.

- Build strong cross-functional relationships and influence without authority to drive consistent execution.

10) Budget & Resource Management

- Manage the safety budget for AES Indiana and AES Ohio, ensuring effective resource allocation and prioritization.

- Build business cases for critical risk reduction investments (process, training, technology, equipment).

Key Interfaces

- Utility Presidents / COO / Operations leadership

- Generation, T&D, and Construction/Capital Delivery leadership teams

- Program/Project Management, Engineering, and Central Operations

- Enterprise EHS CoE, Risk, Legal, HR, Supply Chain, Finance, Digital/IT

- Contractors, vendors, and external partners

- Regulators and local/state agencies

Required Qualifications

- 10+ years progressive safety leadership experience in utilities, power generation, T&D, heavy industrial, or similar high-risk operations , including multi-site accountability.

- Demonstrated success improving serious incident prevention and operational safety performance.

- Strong working knowledge of OSHA regulatory frameworks; experience managing audits and regulatory interactions.

- Experience leading incident investigations and implementing sustainable corrective actions.

- Proven ability to influence senior leaders and drive cross-functional change at scale.

Preferred Qualifications

- Professional certification(s): CSP, CIH, CHMM, CPEA, or equivalent.

- Experience in regulated utility environments and union/contractor-heavy workforces.

- Experience deploying safety management systems and digital EHS tools (incident management, audits, action tracking, analytics).

Leadership Competencies

- Visible, field-oriented safety leadership; high accountability with strong empathy

- Clear, concise communicator across frontline to executive levels

- Strong judgment under pressure; disciplined decision-making

- Systems thinking, continuous improvement mindset, and operational rigor

- Ability to lead through influence and build alignment across diverse stakeholders

Work Environment & Travel

AES Clean Energy is recruiting for the position of Market Lead within the Transmission Strategy department. The Transmission Strategy department is responsible for performing transmission system analysis to steer AES Clean Energy greenfield prospecting efforts and support the interconnection for our large utility-scale project portfolio.  This is an outstanding opportunity for individual who is passionate about renewable energy and seeking high-growth work environment.  The Transmission Strategy department actively tracks and analyzes transmission systems not just as they exist today, but how they will exist in the future. The department is instrumental in the strategic siting efforts of the entire development platform. The position will be responsible to set up and run a variety of innovative, automated power flow studies using power flow and coding software. As an internal power flow study expert, this position will work with internal Strategic Development team, and external entities including Transmission Owners, ISO/RTO to review, analyze and replicate generator interconnection study results.

The person could be based in one of our EAST region offices or work remotely. Some travel will be required (~10%).

Principal Duties and Responsibilities :
In partnership with internal stakeholders, lead to the successful execution of both new and acquired projects across the United States.

- Analyze transmission grid to identify new opportunities for interconnecting renewable energy projects (i.e. solar, storage, wind).

- Spearhead power flow analysis such as First Contingency Incremental Transfer Capability (FCITC), injection analysis, replicating key market and region deliverability studies.

- Ability to set up and conduct automated power flow analysis using Python, or other scripting languages to expedite the analysis process.

- Perform injection studies to identify the optimal interconnection locations for the placement of generator resources across the targeted study/focus region.

- Actively track and participate in regions Transmission Planning Process, and advocate for AES clean energy portfolio to be included in Long Term Planning process.

- Experience personally running nodal production modeling (i.e., PROMOD, UPLAN, GE MAPS, Aurora), and evaluating dispatch trends, curtailment trends and locational marginal pricing trends.

- Obtain, update, and maintain regional power flow base cases with changes in resource mix and transmission topology based on ISO/RTO regional plans.

- Remain up to date on all relevant new and upcoming technologies and knowledge to model them as per regions generator interconnection study criteria.

- Perform network upgrade cost estimate allocation for the proposed projects, based upon applicable tariff.

- Verify and challenge study results. Perform multiple scenario sensitivity analysis based on future queue projections and retirements.

- Perform study review and provide technical insight and decision on acquisition generator projects.

- Strong knowledge of market efficiency analysis and identifying least congestion transmission points in the grid for delivery of power for PPA.

- Understand and gain proficiency in Transmission Providers’ tariff, business practices, interconnection standards, interconnection study practices, cost allocation methodologies, transmission planning standards, and transmission system performance evaluation criteria. Possess an understanding of regional transmission plans and operational practices.

Minimum Qualifications :

- BS in Electrical Engineering or related field.

- +7 years of working experience in renewable or traditional energy development, or transmission planning with an emphasis on generator interconnection studies.

- Proficiency in power flow software (TARA, PSS/E).

- Ability to automate generator interconnection studies on an interconnection wide basis.

- Extensive knowledge of PJM Regional Transmission Expansion Plan (RTEP), Long Term Transmission Planning Process and modeling methodology.

- Extensive knowledge of PJM Generator Interconnection study methodology.

Desired Skills and Expertise:

- MS in Electrical Engineering or related field.

- Familiarity with transmission systems and expansion plans, and generator interconnection study methodologies in MISO, NYISO and other affected systems.

- Strong organizational skills and ability to prioritize and manage several projects simultaneously to meet project schedules.

AES Clean Energy , a leading independent power producer with one of the largest renewable energy portfolios in the U.S., is seeking a NERC Operations Senior Analyst.  Reporting to the NERC Operations Team Leader, the NERC Operations Senior Analyst supports the company’s NERC Operations & Planning (O&P) compliance program by executing day-to-day tasks that ensure all operations and maintenance activities meet North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) reliability standards. This role focuses on maintaining compliance through diligent monitoring, evidence collection, audit support, regulatory research, and cross-functional collaboration. The NERC Operations Analyst plays a critical part in upholding the reliability and security of the Bulk Electric System by working closely with the Team Leader and various teams to embed best practices in reliability and regulatory compliance across the organization.
Key Responsibilities:

- O&P Implementation: Support implementation of O&M compliance processes and field activities for key applicable NERC O&P standards (e.g. FAC, PRC, EOP, MOD). Maintain relationships with field operations personnel to allow consistently completing monthly compliance checklist and confirming consistent implementation of compliance. Execute the Milestones and Project Manage the Timelines for Execution of Ops Compliance standards.  Directly support the submission of data needed from AES Tools/SCADA to deliver to Regulatory Entities.

- Evidence Gathering & Audit Support: Collect, organize, and provide compliance evidence (maintenance records, logs, test results, etc.) to NERC Compliance team to demonstrate adherence to NERC requirements. Assist in audit preparation and submission of supporting data requests, compiling documentation (e.g. Reliability Standard Audit Worksheets), and supporting regulatory inspections and NERC audits under the guidance of the Team Leader.

- Regulatory Updates & Analysis: Work closely with NERC Compliance team to provide input to changing NERC Reliability Standards and regional/ISO requirements . Collaborate changes to the standards with different business units to ensure AES is ready to come into compliance with the new/revised Reliability Standard. Escalate any challenges in implementation in a timely manner to ensure compliance.

- Cross-Functional Coordination: Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams – Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Project Development, Regulatory Affairs, IT/OT Security, NERC Compliance etc. – to integrate NERC compliance seamlessly into all stages of the asset life cycle.  View compliance through a solutions-based lens helping groups develop systems to achieve compliance. Ensure appropriate transition of compliance evidence for new projects from execution team to operations team. Ensure appropriate QC is performed and work with NERC Compliance team in developing future periodic tasks for future compliance. Ensure that changes in plant configuration or operational control follow a robust Management of Change process that addresses NERC compliance impacts. Facilitate regular cross-departmental meetings or working groups to review compliance status, address gaps, and share best practices, thereby fostering an enterprise-wide commitment to compliance. Validate the execution of NERC Compliance standards impacting SCADA Alarm Standards and HMIs to meet NERC Guidance, Recommendations, and Standards.  Assume responsibilities of OATI User to deliver NERC GADS data submitted through OATI Portal.  Establish optimal mapping of PRC compliance requirements for PSMP sheets to SAP Maintenance Plans, FLOCs, and Equipment.

- Procedure Training & Implementation: Work with the internal operational departments to ensure the agreed procedure for NERC Compliance Standards is appropriately understood by all members of the team and ensure consistent implementation of the procedure. Identify needs for consistent evidence development and work with NERC Compliance team to ensure templates for relevant NERC Compliance standards are developed and implemented.

- Issue Management & Continuous Improvement: Help investigate potential reliability risks and perform initial analysis of incidents or near-misses in collaboration with NERC Compliance Team. Identify opportunities to improve compliance processes or tools, such as enhancing evidence management systems or internal control measures, to drive efficiency and robust NERC compliance.

Qualifications and Experience:

- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Energy Management, or a related field (required).

- Experience: Mid-level professional with approximately 3–7+ years of experience in Inverter Based Resource operations, maintenance, testing . Experience in a generator owner/operator environment or renewable energy projects is a strong plus.

- NERC Standard Implementation Knowledge: Experience in designing and implementing controls related FAC-008, EOP-012, PRC -004, PRC-005, PRC-028, PRC-029, PRC-030 etc. Working knowledge related to Transmission Planning or Protection and Control.

- Analytical & Organizational Skills: Detail-oriented with strong analytical abilities for reviewing technical data and compliance evidence. Excellent organizational and time-management skills to handle multiple compliance tasks, documentation requirements, and strict deadlines. Proficiency in using office productivity tools and compliance management systems for tracking standards, evidence, and audits.

- Communication & Teamwork: Effective written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly convey compliance requirements and technical information to cross-functional teams. Strong interpersonal skills and a collaborative attitude, with experience working across departments (e.g. O&M, Engineering, Regulatory) to achieve common goals. A proactive, self-motivated approach with a commitment to professional integrity and continuous improvement in reliability compliance practices.

-

Preferred Qualifications (Optional):

- Certifications: NERC System Operator Certification (e.g., Reliability Coordinator level) or demonstrating a strong understanding of grid reliability operations. A Professional Engineer (PE) license or Project Management Professional (PMP) certification is a plus, reflecting advanced technical and project management skills in a compliance context.

- Additional Skills: Experience with compliance audits or regulatory inspections (NERC, Regional Entities, or FERC) is beneficial. Familiarity with Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) tools and data analytics for tracking compliance obligations is advantageous. An understanding of continuous improvement or risk management methodologies (e.g., Lean Six Sigma ) in operations or compliance programs is also appreciated.

Position Overview:
AES Clean Energy , a leading independent power producer with one of the largest renewable energy portfolios in the U.S. , is seeking a NERC Operations Team Leader to serve as the company’s subject matter expert (SME) on North American Electric Reliability Corporation ( NERC ) standards. In this key role, you will manage the execution of NERC regulatory requirements across all operations and maintenance (O&M) activities for our fleet of clean energy assets, ensuring full compliance with applicable Reliability Standards and driving operational excellence. Reporting to the Senior Director of Operations and Performance Management, you will act as the primary SME contact and to internal teams (O&M, Engineering, etc.), guiding them in interpreting and adhering to NERC O&P (Operations & Planning) standards and instilling a culture of reliability and compliance across the organization. This position offers the opportunity to support AES’s rapidly growing renewable portfolio – including utility-scale solar, wind, battery storage, and other clean energy projects – and to play a pivotal role in maintaining the reliability and security of the Bulk Electric System while upholding industry-leading best practices . You will also lead a team of NERC Operations SME professionals and collaborate cross-functionally to support NERC compliance in day-to-day operations.
Key Responsibilities:

- NERC Operations Program Leadership: Oversee day-to-day NERC compliance execution for all AES Clean Energy Operational sites. Act as an Operations Standard SME for NERC Compliance Standards like Facility Ratings, Protection and Control, Emergency Operations and Voltage regulation.

- Regulatory Compliance Execution: Partner with Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Protection and Control, Asset Management and NERC Compliance Teams to translate NERC regulatory requirements into executable processes, technical controls, maintenance programs and audit ready evidence. Document and ensure rigorous adherence to all AES NERC Compliance procedures relevant NERC O&P standards (e.g. FAC, PRC, EOP, VAR standards) in the operation and maintenance of generation assets, as well as compliance with any applicable Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), regional entity (e.g., MRO, WECC, SERC) and ISO requirements. Oversee the Milestones and Project Manage the Timelines for Execution of Ops Compliance standards.  Directly support the submission of data needed from AES Tools/SCADA to deliver to Regulatory Entities.  Validate the Execution of NERC Compliance standards impacting SCADA Alarm Standards and HMIs to meet NERC Guidance, Recommendations, and Standards.  Assume responsibilities of OATI Security Officer to oversee NERC GADS data submitted through OATI Portal.  Manage Analyst for submission of NERC GADS data through OATI Portal.  Establish optimal mapping of PRC compliance requirements for PSMP sheets to SAP Maintenance Plans, FLOCs, and Equipment.

- Audit & Evidence Management: Serve as SME in all NERC compliance audits, self-certifications, spot checks, and investigations , both internal and external. Collaborate with NERC Compliance team in the preparation and submission of comprehensive compliance evidence and documentation, including Reliability Standard Audit Worksheets (RSAWs) , procedures, one-line diagrams, maintenance records, and operating logs. Ensure an organized evidence repository and robust record-keeping practices for all compliance obligations.

- Internal Controls & Risk Management: Assess reliability risk associated with implementation of existing NERC Compliance Standard specific procedures and develop internal controls to mitigate reliability risks.

- Procedure Training & Implementation: Work with the internal operational departments to ensure the agreed procedure for NERC Compliance Standards is appropriately understood by all members of the team and ensure consistent implementation of the procedure. Identify needs for consistent evidence development and work with NERC Compliance team to ensure templates for relevant NERC Compliance standards are developed and implemented.

Ensure appropriate transition of compliance evidence for new projects from execution team to operations team. Ensure appropriate QC is performed and work with NERC Compliance team in developing future periodic tasks for future compliance. Ensure that changes in plant configuration or operational control follow a robust Management of Change process that addresses NERC compliance impacts. Facilitate regular cross-departmental meetings or working groups to review compliance status, address gaps, and share best practices, thereby fostering an enterprise-wide commitment to compliance.  View compliance with a solutions-based mindset focused not only providing the requirements, but assisting cross functional teams develop practical and efficient systems to comply with them.

- Leadership & Team Management: Lead and mentor the NERC Operations team , setting clear goals and providing ongoing coaching and development opportunities. Manage personnel performance, establish role clarity and accountability, and cultivate an environment of continuous improvement and collaboration. As a people leader, provide direction and support for direct reports in their day-to-day activities and career growth, and ensure that the team’s structure and skills grow in step with the company’s expanding portfolio and evolving regulatory landscape.

- Strategic Planning & Continuous Improvement: Contribute to long-term compliance strategy and planning for AES Clean Energy. Work with the Director of NERC Compliance and other leaders to set compliance objectives that align with corporate goals and industry developments.

Required Qualifications:

- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Energy Management, or a related technical field (B.S. or equivalent experience required) . An advanced degree (M.S., MBA) in a relevant field is a plus but not required.

- Experience: 5+ years of experience in the electric power industry, with a focus on power generation operations, maintenance, or NERC compliance (8+ years preferred) .

- Technical Knowledge: Strong technical knowledge in implementing compliance for NERC Reliability standards like PRC-005, FAC-008, EOP-012, PRC-004, PRC-028, PRC-029 and PRC-030.  Familiarity with the Bulk Electric System and power plant operations (generation plant equipment, protection systems, relays, SCADA systems, inverter-based resources, etc.) is essential. Ability to interpret engineering documents (one-line diagrams, protection schemes, planning studies, etc.) and understand their compliance implications is expected.

- Leadership & Communication: Excellent leadership and interpersonal skills , with a track record of building high-performance teams and cross-functional partnerships. Ability to effectively communicate complex technical and regulatory information to diverse audiences – from field technicians to executives – in a clear, concise manner. Strong organizational and project management skills to prioritize tasks, manage multiple compliance activities, and meet firm deadlines. Self-motivated and proactive in identifying what needs to be done, with the drive to see tasks through to completion without significant guidance . High attention to detail and analytical skills for problem-solving and process improvement in a compliance context.

Familiarity with the end-to-end project life cycle of generation assets – from design and grid interconnection through operations – as it relates to NERC compliance is highly valued.

A Professional Engineer (P.E.) license in a relevant discipline and/or a Project Management Professional (PMP) certification are also preferred, reflecting advanced technical and project management expertise.

Job Description

Support the design, configuration, implementation, and maintenance of Distribution Management System (DMS), SCADA, Outage Management System (OMS), and related operational technology (OT) platforms used to monitor and control the transmission and distribution (T&D) network for DP&L and IPL. These systems are critical to ensuring safe and reliable electric grid operations.
The role requires foundational knowledge of hardware and software systems, T&D operations, networking, and cybersecurity, with exposure to power system modeling and remote field devices. The engineer will work with both modern and legacy technologies while supporting the AES Digital Strategy.

Key Responsibilities:

- Assist in the configuration, installation, and maintenance of OT systems to support reliable grid operations.

- Support the development and maintenance of data models for ADMS power system applications.

- Help configure and support advanced applications such as Distribution Power Flow (DPF), Fault Location, Isolation & Service Restoration (FLISR), and Volt/VAR Control (VVC).

- Collaborate on integrating Geographic Information System (GIS) data into ADMS by supporting data extraction, translation, and loading processes.

- Provide support for daily operations of OT systems used by T&D field teams, engineering, planning, reporting, and dispatch.

- Assist in troubleshooting issues and escalating complex problems to senior engineers as needed.

- Work with cross-functional teams to support OT applications and improve system performance.

- Partner with internal stakeholders to understand business needs and contribute to process improvements through technology.

- Support documentation efforts, including diagrams of current and future OT architectures.

- Participate in testing, deployment, and validation of system updates and enhancements.

- Stay informed on applicable regulations and support compliance activities.

- Participate in the OT team’s on-call rotation (as required, typically with supervision during initial period).

- Support vendor coordination and assist in evaluating tools and solutions.

- Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field (preferred ABET-accredited institution).

- 1–3 years of relevant experience (internships or academic projects in power systems or OT are a plus).

- Basic understanding of power systems, SCADA, or industrial control systems.

- Foundational knowledge of hardware, software, and networking concepts.

- Interest in learning about real-time T&D control systems and OT environments.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

- Good written and verbal communication skills.

- Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and learn from senior engineers.
